name: Dumbbell Spider Curl
movementPattern: Elbow flexion - prone torso, vertical upper arms
grip: Supinated, palms facing forward at the bottom and upward toward the shoulders as the elbows flex.
description: Curl two dumbbells while lying chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging vertically in front of the support pad.
setup: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline of roughly 45 degrees above horizontal.
Lie prone with the chest and stomach supported against the backrest, upper chest near the top edge, and feet braced on the floor behind you.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and let both arms hang straight down toward the floor with palms facing forward.
instructions: Keep the chest pressed into the pad and upper arms hanging vertically.
Flex both elbows to curl the dumbbells upward in an arc toward the shoulders.
Pause briefly near peak elbow flexion without lifting the chest off the bench or driving the elbows forward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to the hanging start position under full control.
cues: Keep the chest heavy on the pad.
Let the upper arms hang straight down.
Curl through the elbows without swinging.
commonMistakes: Pushing the chest up off the incline pad to create momentum.
Pulling the elbows backward into a row or swinging the upper arms forward at the top.

logging.example: Two 10 kg dumbbells: record 10 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Keep the same equipment variant and record the mass of a single dumbbell rather than the combined pair. EZ-bar or barbell spider curls use total bar mass and should be logged as a separate exercise.

variantNote: Assumption: bilateral dumbbell spider curl lying prone on an ~45-degree incline bench rather than over the vertical side of a preacher pad or with an EZ-bar/barbell.
reviewNotes: Confirm whether your consumer catalog maps generic 'Spider Curl' to dumbbells on an incline bench or an EZ-bar on a vertical preacher pad.
In the left panel, the near hand retains a slightly neutral wrist angle while the far hand shows supination; keep at draft until trainer/equipment review.
